correctness.rationale: Exact uniform GL_m character sums for rank-zero/one/two test matrices follow by a stated subspace-Möbius/q-binomial identity and independently agree with Li–Hu 2011, Theorem 2.1. Every Gram entry follows from the rank of a one- or two-cell difference. Orthogonal scalar-color and rook-grid decompositions exhaust exactly 1+m²(q−1) coefficient directions with the stated multiplicities. Explicit factorizations of det H, det(alpha I-H), det(beta I-H), det(gamma I-H) and q^m>1+m(q−1) prove strict positive spectrum, lower mode, and crossover m=2q for every prime power and m≥2. The fixed-q asymptotic follows by eigenvalue expansion. The actual embedded self-contained checker was executed successfully for seven full matrix groups including F4, plus a large finite arithmetic grid; these corroborate only the finite cases and do not substitute for universal proofs.

originality.rationale: Originality is restricted to the precise coefficient Gram spectrum of the constant plus every one-coordinate additive character on GL_m(F_q), its eigenspaces, the sharp gamma-versus-ell_plus crossover at m=2q, and the asymptotic condition number. Known rank-transform eigenvalues (Li–Hu, Delsarte, Kawamura) are mathematical inputs; their inspected relevant statements do not assert this compressed Gram/Riesz classification. Direct searches for GL coordinate-character Gram, rook spectrum, rank-orbit equivalence, exact cutoff, and historical aliases did not identify a source implying the claimed theorem. General harmonic tight-frame theorems concern different character families. This finding does not claim invention of finite-field character sums or rook-graph diagonalization; historical-equivalence risk remains for older association-scheme specializations. Search absence alone is not treated as proof of originality.

value.rationale: This is a complete, naturally parametrized exact spectral and sharp stability classification of constant and all one-coordinate Fourier measurements on the classical nonlinear finite-field variety GL_m, with every equality mode. It exposes a strict dimension-to-field-size switch m=2q in the maximizing eigendirection, and sharp large-dimension conditioning asymptotics. This precise infinite-family Riesz invariant is mathematically motivated by reliable low-complexity Fourier measurements; it is not a renaming of rank-transform inputs, an arbitrary small finite slice, or a claim about general Fourier bases.
